I have resolved the issue where `JSONField` lookups `has_key`, `has_keys`, and `has_any_keys` failed to handle numeric keys on SQLite, MySQL, and Oracle:

- Added [`HasKeyLookup.compile_json_path_final_key()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-h767rwid/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L175-L177) in [django/db/models/fields/json.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-h767rwid/django/db/models/fields/json.py) so that [`HasKeyLookup.as_sql()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-h767rwid/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L179-L209) always compiles the final key as a JSON object key (`."<key>"`) rather than an array index (`[<index>]`), while still compiling any intermediate `KeyTransform` path segments via [`compile_json_path()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-h767rwid/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L129-L139).
- Added [`HasKeyOrArrayIndex`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-h767rwid/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L257-L259) and updated [`KeyTransformIsNull`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-h767rwid/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L393-L414) and [`KeyTransformExact.as_oracle()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-h767rwid/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L471-L483) to use it so key transforms on array indices continue to compile as array index lookups.
